points.description: States that a linear classifier cannot classify data whose classes are not linearly separable in the feature space (it only forms linear/straight-line/hyperplane boundaries).
points.partial_credit: Half only if the limitation is stated but the term 'linearly separable' (or equivalent non-separable feature-space idea) is missing or imprecise.

points.description: States that a nonlinear discriminant function classifier can handle such non-linearly separable cases because it creates more complex (nonlinear/curved) decision boundaries.
points.partial_credit: Half only if it says nonlinear handles complex data but does not mention decision boundaries.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both: the linear classifier fails when classes are not linearly separable, and the nonlinear one succeeds by forming more complex decision boundaries. Vague claims like 'nonlinear is more accurate' or 'works better' earn nothing. A wrong statement within a point (e.g. saying nonlinear is simpler or faster) means that point earns 0.
